kills.property: After a deposit of value v, the depositor's recorded balance in C equals the deposited amount (balances reflect deposits).
kills.change_summary: Delete the statement 'balances[msg.sender]+= msg.value;' so deposits never update the balance.

kills.property: After Deposit with value v, the caller's recorded balance increases by exactly v (not a constant 1).
kills.change_summary: Credit a constant 1 instead of msg.value: 'balances[msg.sender]+= 1;'.

kills.property: Depositing twice accumulates: the balance after a second deposit equals the sum of both deposits.
kills.change_summary: Replace the accumulation 'balances[msg.sender]+= msg.value;' with an assignment 'balances[msg.sender]= msg.value;', so prior balance is lost.

kills.property: After a successful SetMinSum(_val) call on an uninitialized contract, MinSum() equals _val.
kills.change_summary: Delete the statement 'MinSum = _val;' so SetMinSum no longer changes MinSum.

kills.property: After any sequence of SetMinSum calls before initialization, MinSum equals the value of the last call (it is overwritten, not accumulated).
kills.change_summary: Change the assignment to 'MinSum += _val;' so SetMinSum adds to the existing MinSum instead of overwriting it.

kills.property: Once the contract is initialized, SetMinSum can no longer change MinSum: MinSum keeps its first set value (calls may revert but never alter it), while the mutant lets any later SetMinSum overwrite MinSum.
kills.change_summary: Remove the 'if(intitalized)revert();' guard so SetMinSum also updates MinSum after initialization.

kills.property: For any uninitialized state and any fuzzed caller/value, calling SetMinSum(_val) stores exactly _val in MinSum; the mutant stores _val+1, breaking the rule for some input.
kills.change_summary: Replace the assignment `MinSum = _val;` with `MinSum = _val + 1;` so the stored MinSum differs.
